name: fuel_issue_notify_department
description: Handoff tool for a spec handoff whose recipientResolution.targetType is 'department' (the same shape covers 'branch'/'designation' — swap the table/field names). Resolves the department name to an id, fetches every ACTIVE employee in it, and notifies all of them (whenMultiple: 'notify_all') via send_bulk_template_message. When the department can't be resolved, or resolves to zero active employees, the requestor is told the spec's fallbackReply instead — nobody is left thinking the handoff went through silently. stateParams always carries: notified (boolean), recipientCount (number). success is always true: a message is guaranteed to reach someone (the department, or the requestor via the fallback), so this step never blocks the conversation — successMode 'always' in the calling step's contract.

phoneNumber.description: Requestor's WhatsApp number, used only for the fallback message

issueNumber.description: Reference number collected earlier in the flow, sent to the department

requestorName.description: Requestor's display name from system context

workflowDefinition.description: Resolve the 'Fuel' department by name, fetch its active employees, and bulk-notify them; fall back to telling the requestor when the department or its employees can't be found.

nodes.name: Look up the Fuel department by name
Check whether the department exists
Only look up employees when the department resolved

trueBranch.name: Fetch active employees in the department
Build the recipient list from the envelope
Only bulk-notify when at least one employee matched

falseBranch.name: Tell the requestor nobody is in the department
Tell the requestor the department isn't configured

nodes.name: Build the result the engine reads

__annotations.why_this_example_exists: The worked pattern for recipientResolution.targetType 'department' (identical shape for 'branch'/'designation' — only the table name and the id field on employee change: branchId / designationId). Demonstrates: (1) resolve name -> id first, guard on zero rows before ever touching step 2 — a departmentId of '' would otherwise silently match employee rows with departmentId: null in some ORMs, which is exactly the kind of bug this two-step shape is written to avoid by being explicit; (2) whenMultiple: 'notify_all' maps to send_bulk_template_message, built from the SAME db_read_records shape used everywhere else in this registry — no bespoke org-chart tool was invented; (3) every branch — department not found, department found but empty, department found with matches — ends in exactly one message being sent, so the requestor is never left without an answer (the fallbackReply requirement in the spec schema exists precisely so this never gets skipped); (4) the result node is FLAT (success, message, stateParams, no top-level data/result/type) and returns success: true on every path, because a message always went somewhere — the calling step's contract must declare successMode: 'always'; 'notified' in stateParams is what a later step (or an audit trail) reads to know which outcome actually happened; (5) db_read_records' filters are a literal Prisma where clause — { name: { equals, mode: 'insensitive' } } and { departmentId, status } are passed through unmodified, accountId is a separate top-level param the tool merges in itself, never hand-added to filters.
__annotations.notify_one_arbitrary_variant: For recipientResolution.whenMultiple: 'notify_one_arbitrary', skip check_employees' recipients array and guard_employees_found's send_bulk_template_message branch; instead send_template_message directly to '$fetch_employees.data[0].phoneNumber' inside a single if-else guarding on employeeCount > 0, and record recipientCount as 0 or 1 in stateParams. Only use this variant once the spec has confirmed exactly one person is expected to hold that department/branch/designation.
__annotations.manager_variant: For recipientResolution.targetType 'manager', replace resolve_department/check_department/guard_department_found/fetch_employees/check_employees entirely with a single get_employee_manager_info tool node ({ phoneNumber: "$input.body.phoneNumber" }) followed by a code node reading success and managerDetails.managerPhoneNumber, then the same guard_employees_found-shaped if-else on whether a manager was found.
__annotations.expected_validator_warning: mcp__orchestrator__validate_tools warns that build_final_response's $("check_employees") reference is inside guard_department_found.trueBranch and may not have run. This is deliberate, the same discipline mr_save_request.json's branch_reference_note documents: the code reads `$("check_employees") || {}` and every field access goes through `|| 0`/`=== true`, so the false path (department never found) reads as employeeCount: 0, notified: false — exactly the fallback outcome, never a crash. Read every warning like this one and confirm the guard exists before accepting it; do not silence it by restructuring the graph.
